Introduce a small nonrefundable attempted-read ledger in each owned observer reader. It has a fixed declared limit, monotonically charged attempts and no refund on faults. Before each OS read, choose a positive requested size no greater than65536, the remaining shared attempted-read allowance, and the remaining admitted per-file length plus at most one explicitly budgeted EOF/probe byte. Charge the requested size before the OS read. Retain that charge if the call returns fewer bytes, EOF or throws. Conservative request accounting is permitted and must be labeled requested/attempted bytes, rather than successful consumed bytes. If no positive allowance remains, decline without another OS read; never increase a cap to obtain an EOF probe.

Use fstat length admission to reject a mismatching exact pin before streaming where that pin is available. The stream must still detect growth/truncation/content/descriptor changes with before/after identity and SHA256. Require exactly the admitted number of content bytes and, when an EOF check is used, reserve its probe before reading. A shared cap can conservatively decline a permitted input at its boundary; no completeness promise is added. Empty files still need descriptor/identity checks, and any read/probe remains accounted. All read calls in SDK19, Python explicit modules and external-anchor initial/boundary validation must pass their correct ledger. The separately bounded interpreter image retains its original maximum and uses its own finite ledger if the same streaming routine now requires one.
